children: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has added eight new members to the US Preventive Services Task Force, a scientifically independent panel that makes decisions on the types of medical screenings health insurers must cover.
The body now has 16 members, who serve four-year terms.
The appointments come after RFK Jr. dismissed two former members in May,
a review "to protect the integrity of the task force’s work."
Among the new appointees is chair Seth J. Corey, a pediatric hematologist-oncologist affiliated with the Cleveland Clinic.
Other new members are at least two individuals who have been critical of COVID-19 vaccines or indicated not as many people need them,

reported. Several are specialists rather than primary care and prevention experts who have typically been selected. New appointee Stephen T. Parente is not an MD and previously served as a health economics adviser to President Trump.
The task force last met in person in March 2025. Since then, other scheduled meetings of the group have been cancelled four times. It usually convenes three times a year.

title: RFK Jr. appoints new members to US Preventive Services Task Force
